messages.subject: WAIC Calculations in Stan
parts:
In a recent thread about the syntax of Stan as a language, Bob made the following statement about WAIC:

We're also working toward more finely articulating the log probability
function itself, such as splitting out the likelihood from the prior,
so that we can define WAIC (a nicer alternative to DIC) and splitting
up the data into batches so that we can use stochastic and parallel
inferences of various sorts.

What exactly is meant by "splitting the likelihood from the prior?" From the way I understood WAIC as defined in Gelman et al. (2014, pp. 173–174), one can calculate the WAIC using Stan in the following way:
  1. In the generated quantities block, capture the likelihood at each point individually for every collected sample (for loop onto a vector, for example)
  2. Once the sampling is done, calculate:
    1. The log of the pointwise mean likelihoods [2.1]
    2. The sample variance of the logs of the point-wise likelihoods (pWAIC2) [2.2]
  3. Calculate -2 * {sum ([2.1]) - sum([2.2])}

Was all that was meant that instead of manually capturing the point-wise likelihoods (which, for the built-in distributions need exponentiation as only log-densities are defined) there will be an option to block collect them, or am I exhibiting a deeper misunderstanding of the process.

For clarification, here is sample Stan code which should collect the point-wise likelihoods:

generated quantities {
  vector[N] PointPosteriors;          // vector for computing log pointwise predictive density
  for (i in 1:N) {
    PointPosteriors[i] <- exp(lognormal_log(LR[i], mu, sigma));
  }
}

One vector per collected sample is captured and appended to a large matrix in the resulting Stan object. Given that matrix of sample likelihoods, an R function which should return the WAIC would be:


WAIC <- function(pointMatrix) {
  lppd <- sum(log(apply(pointMatrix, 2, FUN = mean)))
  pWAIC2 <- sum(apply(log(pointMatrix), 2, FUN = var))
  return(-2 * (lppd - pWAIC2))
}

I'd certainly appreciate being confirmed or corrected in my understanding; thanks!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] WAIC Calculations in Stan
parts:
On Mar 7, 2014, at 6:01 PM, Avraham Adler <avraha...@gmail.com> wrote:

>
> In a recent thread about the syntax of Stan as a language, Bob made the following statement about WAIC:
>
> We're also working toward more finely articulating the log probability
> function itself, such as splitting out the likelihood from the prior,
> so that we can define WAIC (a nicer alternative to DIC) and splitting
> up the data into batches so that we can use stochastic and parallel
> inferences of various sorts.
>
> What exactly is meant by "splitting the likelihood from the prior?"

Just having ways to label the components of a model. Perhaps having
them computed in their own blocks. That still won't necessarily solve
the problem of needing the individual likelihoods for each data item
needed for WAIC.

> From the way I understood WAIC as defined in Gelman et al. (2014, pp. 173–174), one can calculate the WAIC using Stan in the following way:
> • In the generated quantities block, capture the likelihood at each point individually for every collected sample (for loop onto a vector, for example)
> • Once the sampling is done, calculate:
> • The log of the pointwise mean likelihoods [2.1]
> • The sample variance of the logs of the point-wise likelihoods (pWAIC2) [2.2]
> • Calculate -2 * {sum ([2.1]) - sum([2.2])}
> Was all that was meant that instead of manually capturing the point-wise likelihoods (which, for the built-in distributions need exponentiation as only log-densities are defined) there will be an option to block collect them, or am I exhibiting a deeper misunderstanding of the process.

Right --- that's all I meant. But we're not sure we're going to do
it this way because the capture in generated quantities is going to be
more efficient.

- Bob
